A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same attention-sink study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original measurements of pretrained models and controlled pre-training experiments, including attention-sink metrics, validation losses and architectural ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original positional-embedding interventions, downstream evaluations, optimization controls and supervised fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: Appendix D.4 introduces and trains p-normalized softmax and sigmoid variants, replacing sum normalization with an Lp-style normalizer. This extends the attention procedures studied; the existing key-bias and unnormalized-sigmoid designs remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds HellaSwag downstream evaluation in Appendix C.3 and UltraChat supervised fine-tuning in Appendix E. These extend coverage beyond the retained Pile domains and synthetic-token analyses to downstream task performance and conversational adaptation.

E2.justification: Figure 29 adds p-normalized softmax and sigmoid variants to comparisons with unnormalized sigmoid attention. The existing attention-bias and kernel comparison sets in Tables 4 and 6 remain unchanged; newly cited mitigation methods are not thereby evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include learning-rate comparisons with compensating training durations up to 80k steps, GPT2 positional-embedding interventions, HellaSwag accuracy metrics, and one-epoch full-model SFT with loss and gradient-norm monitoring. Separately, the normalization-scale entry changes from 0.02 in v1 Table 11 to 0.05 in v2 Table 14 while its outcomes remain unchanged; this establishes a reported setting correction, not a demonstrated rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of GPT2 positional-embedding replacement/swapping, learning rate versus training duration, data scarcity versus overfitting, downstream-performance relationships, alternative normalizers and SFT stability. These substantially expand the mechanistic and robustness evidence. The key-bias dimensionality analysis already existed and is relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Averaging attention-sink measurements over sampled sequences is retained without introducing uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports GPT2 positional-intervention results, Jamba sink rates of 88.48% and 87.88%, and optimization, HellaSwag, normalization and SFT findings. For example, Table 9 reports 6.29% sink and 3.67 validation loss at learning rate 1e-4 over 80k steps. Most matched earlier scores, including the 1B softmax/sigmoid comparison, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 revises the SGD-like normalization-scaling argument and adds an AdamW derivation with optimizer-specific learning-rate, epsilon and weight-decay transformations (Appendix D.4, Equations 36–42). Equations 43–44 define p-normalization and derive its temperature/root representation. The original repeated-token propositions are retained.

C1.justification: The central claims about effective optimization, sufficient data, sink position, non-informative key biases and attention-score dependence remain. The unnormalized-sigmoid finding up to 1B parameters is retained. Explicitly saying 'auto-regressive' in v2's abstract clarifies scope already stated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the learning-rate effect as persisting beyond slower optimization and attributes the reduced-data behavior to data amount rather than overfitting. It links GPT2 sink position to the first learned positional embedding and discusses why stronger sinks need not imply better cross-family performance. Section 8 newly identifies downstream benefit as unresolved.

D1.justification: v2 adds TinyLlama/RegMix implementation provenance, Jamba model identifiers, the downstream evaluation framework, and UltraChat/alignment-handbook references with SFT hyperparameters. These improve documentation without establishing a change to the retained implementation. The principal code link and default pre-training specification remain.

R1.justification: A new four-part related-work appendix connects attention sinks with entropy collapse, activation outliers, mitigation methods and applications. It substantially expands engagement with work including Bondarenko, Guo, Kaul, Zhai and Ramapuram, and explicitly credits earlier observations of small sink-token keys or values.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. v2 condenses Section 7.3, moves detailed key-bias discussion into the appendix, adds related-work and post-training appendix sections, and makes localized terminology, attribution and header edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial displays for positional interventions, learning-rate controls, downstream performance, Jamba, training dynamics, normalization and SFT. It splits v1 Table 5, moving its lower portion to Table 13, and relocates early figures. The small-LLaMA norm visualization in v1 Figure 14 is removed; most other existing displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The longer-training controls in Table 9 address an important alternative explanation for v1's learning-rate finding. Positional interventions and normalization experiments strengthen the mechanistic evidence, while the AdamW derivation and expanded related work improve technical grounding and attribution. These gains substantially strengthen the study despite removal of one diagnostic visualization. Downstream benefit remains unresolved, appropriately acknowledged in v2.
